english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{1+\cos^{2}x}$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_{0}^{T}f(x)\,dx$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\dfrac{\sin^{2}x}{1+\cos^{2}x}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_{0}^{T}f(x)\,dx$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $f$ has period $\pi$; for $n\pi\le T<(n+1)\pi$: $nA\le\int_0^Tf\le(n+1)A$ with $A=\int_0^{\pi}f$, so the limit is $\frac{A}{\pi}$
$f(\pi-x)=f(x)$, so $A=2\int_0^{\pi/2}f$ (this also keeps $\tan x$ continuous on $[0,\frac{\pi}{2})$)
solution_full: $f(x+\pi)=f(x)$, so $f$ is periodic with period $\pi$; let $A=\int_0^{\pi}f$. For $T>0$ write $n=[T/\pi]$; since $f\ge0$, $nA\le\int_0^{T}f\le(n+1)A$, and $\frac{n\pi}{T}\to1$. Hence the limit equals $\dfrac{A}{\pi}$ (the average over one period).

Since $f(\pi-x)=f(x)$, the property $\int_0^{2a}f=2\int_0^{a}f$ with $a=\frac{\pi}{2}$ gives $A=2\int_0^{\pi/2}f$. Working on $[0,\frac{\pi}{2})$ also avoids the discontinuity of $\tan x$ at $\frac{\pi}{2}$.
The limit is $\dfrac{A}{\pi}=\sqrt2-1=0.4142\ldots$, which is $0.41$ to two decimal places.
originality_note: New: the long-run mean value of a periodic function, where the period integral must be halved by symmetry so that the tan substitution is legitimate (way 5). Closest known: int_0^{n pi} |sin x| dx = 2n and int_0^pi dx/(1 + cos^2 x). Different because: the question is a limit of averages and needs the sandwich nA <= int <= (n+1)A.
blueprint_concepts: Property int(0 to 2a) f(x) dx = 2.int(0 to a) f(x) dx when f(2a - x) = f(x)

concept_use.Property int(0 to 2a) f(x) dx = 2.int(0: f(pi - x) = f(x), so the integral over a period is 2 int_0^{pi/2} f, computed by t = tan x on [0, pi/2).
concept_use.Property for periodic functions: f has period pi, so int_0^T f lies between nA and (n+1)A and the limit is the mean value A/pi.

stem_review: Read as a student: f has domain/codomain; the limit exists (f >= 0 periodic). Checked: (1/pi) int_0^pi f = 0.41421 and the average over [0, 50pi+1] = 0.4128. Answer 0.41 lies between 0 and 1 as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Mean over T tends to the mean over one period pi; that period integral is 2 int_0^{pi/2} f by symmetry, then t = tan x.
justification: Two linked ideas (periodicity with a sandwich argument for the limit, and a symmetry reduction that makes the substitution valid) with a numerical answer. Comparable to 2024-P2-Q13 (L3).
